title: CI runs the macOS job on every push and never cancels a superseded run -- most of the account's Actions spend
body:
## What happens

devbin's CI runs its macOS job (`test-macos` in `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, `runs-on: macos-latest`) on every push to `main`, and nothing cancels a run that a newer push has superseded. devbin's repository is private, where GitHub bills macOS minutes at ten times the Linux rate, so this one job is most of the account's Actions spend.

Measured by vc on 2026-09-21 from the jobs API (each job's start and end, rounded up per job, macOS weighted x10), across the private repositories under matthewsinclair since 2026-07-22: September to date is 9149 weighted minutes, of which devbin's macOS job is 740 minutes, 7400 weighted, about 80%. July, before devbin had CI, was 357. hv reported the account going from never passing the free allowance to about 50 pounds a month, and topped the budget up the same evening so the v0.1.5 cut could make its release object. Not read: GitHub's billing figures (the endpoint needs the `user` scope on gh), and repositories under other organisations.

## Ruling

hv, 2026-09-21: (1) a macOS job runs only on release tags and on demand, never on every push, in devbin and in every repository with macOS artefacts; Ubuntu stays on every push. (2) Every repository cancels superseded runs, not only the macOS ones. (3) devbin goes public, which would make its CI free, but not before it is more stable: October or November. The fleet half of (1) and (2) is tracked on the whiteboard and in intent/wip.md, one estate at a time in its own tree; this issue is devbin's own workflow.

## Fix

- `test-macos` runs on a push of a `v*` tag and on `workflow_dispatch`, and not on a push to `main`. `test-linux` and shellcheck stay on every push. `Test Summary` must still pass on a push to `main` without the macOS leg, and must still require it on a tag.
- `tests.yml` gains a `concurrency` group keyed on the workflow and `github.ref`, with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a newer push to `main` cancels the older run. A tag has its own ref, so its run is never cancelled by a push to `main`.
- `release.yml` is untouched: it already runs on `v*` tags only, on Ubuntu.
- The macOS leg is where `check critic` runs (issue 0077). That gate then runs in CI on tags only; the cut's own gates run it locally on macOS before every release, so no release goes out without it.

## Consequences to state in the docs

- An intermediate pushed commit can get no CI verdict, because a newer push cancelled it. The sweep rule that CI must be green on the pushed commit (vc todo 82) reads on the last pushed commit.
- `docs/releasing.md` says what CI covers on a push and on a tag.

## Tests

`tests/unit/ci-workflow.bats` holds the workflow's shape: its arms that pin the macOS job's triggers and the summary's needs are restated, and new arms hold the tag and dispatch triggers on `test-macos` and the concurrency block. Red first.

## Resolution

Fixed at `993c995`, with `tests/unit/ci-workflow.bats` driven red first: all eight new arms failed against the unchanged workflow, each naming its own reason, and are green after.

Built as specified, with two deliberate departures from the Fix section above, both wider rather than narrower:

- **The concurrency group carries `github.event_name` as well as the workflow and the ref.** The section above named workflow and ref only. A push to `main` and a `workflow_dispatch` on `main` share a ref, so that key would have let a push cancel an on-demand macOS run after its ten-times minutes were spent, and let a dispatch cancel a push's run. Found by cc while building.
- **The macOS condition asks `github.ref_type`, never a tag's spelling**, and `on.push.tags` carries both release forms, `v[0-9]*` and `[0-9]*`. hv ruled one filter for the whole fleet on 2026-09-22 because Utilz has tagged bare since 2.7.0, so a `v*` filter would never have fired there. Verified: Utilz tagged `v1.0.0` through `v2.6.1`, then `2.7.0` through `2.11.0`.

`Test Summary` takes its four inputs through `env` rather than inline expressions, so its decision is a script a test can RUN. vc drove the committed script over 625 combinations of the four inputs against an independently written truth table: no disagreement, a tag with a skipped macOS leg fails, a push with a skipped macOS leg passes, and an unrecognised `MACOS_REQUIRED` refuses by name rather than falling to the permissive branch.

**A `critic-shell` pass over the uncommitted diff found five CRITICAL findings in the arms that the builder and the reviewer had both already accepted, seven of its eight above-threshold findings being in test code rather than in the workflow.** Among them: a refusal asserted to have FIRED but never what it SAID, satisfied by swapping two job names; a `grep "$MACOS"` satisfied by `$MACOS_REQUIRED`; an absence asserted with nothing proving its extractor could match; and a command substitution in a here-document discarding the status of a file it could not read. All are fixed and re-driven, each with its own mutation confirmed applied before its result was read.

Verified by GitHub's own documentation rather than from memory: path filters are not evaluated for pushes of tags, so 0110's board filter cannot suppress a release run; and `github.ref_type` is documented as `branch` or `tag`. actionlint 1.7.12 is clean on both workflows.

Stated limit: these arms hold what the YAML SAYS. What GitHub does with it rests on the documentation plus the first tag pushed under this shape, which does not exist yet. Gtools carries the fleet's first such tag.

Full suite 1600/1600 at `993c995`, 0 not ok, 3 standing skips (`tmp/test/20260922-0834.bats.*`, `.errors` 0 bytes and `.out` carrying `1..1600`), run with no `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS` in the environment, and `git diff HEAD -- lib tests .github docs bin` empty, so the run and the commit are the same bytes. Ships in 0.1.6.
